name: barbell back squat
cue: Bar rests on your upper back with feet about shoulder-width. Brace your core, sit down and back until your thighs are at least parallel, keep your knees in line with your toes, then drive up through your whole foot.

name: goblet squat
cue: Hold one dumbbell vertically at your chest with elbows pointing down. Sit straight down between your knees keeping your chest tall, then stand up by pushing the floor away.

name: bodyweight squat
cue: Feet shoulder-width, arms reaching forward for balance. Sit back and down with your chest up until your thighs are parallel to the floor, then stand.

name: leg press
aliases: leg press machine|45 degree leg press
cue: Place your feet shoulder-width on the platform. Lower until your knees reach about 90 degrees without your lower back lifting off the pad, then press up without locking your knees.

name: bulgarian split squat
aliases: split squat|rear foot elevated split squat
cue: Put your rear foot on a bench or sofa behind you and step the front foot far enough forward that the shin stays near vertical. Lower straight down, then drive through the front heel.

name: walking lunge
cue: Hold dumbbells at your sides and take a long step forward. Lower until both knees are about 90 degrees, then push off the front foot into the next step.

name: reverse lunge
cue: Step one foot back and lower until both knees are around 90 degrees, keeping your torso upright. Push through the front heel to return, then switch legs.

name: step-up
cue: Place one whole foot on a sturdy box or bench. Stand up using the front leg only, without pushing off the back foot, then lower slowly.

name: conventional deadlift
cue: Stand with the bar over mid-foot and hinge down to grip just outside your knees. Brace, push the floor away while keeping the bar against your legs, and finish tall by squeezing your glutes.

name: romanian deadlift
cue: Start standing with the bar at your thighs and soft knees. Push your hips back with a flat back until you feel a strong hamstring stretch, then drive your hips forward to stand.

name: dumbbell romanian deadlift
cue: Hold dumbbells in front of your thighs. Push your hips straight back with a flat back and the weights close to your legs, then squeeze your glutes to stand.

name: hip thrust
cue: Rest your upper back on a bench with the bar over your hips. Drive through your heels until your hips and torso are level, pause for a second, then lower under control.

name: glute bridge
cue: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat. Press through your heels to lift your hips until your body forms a straight line, squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower.

name: barbell bench press
cue: Lie with your shoulder blades pinched back and feet planted. Lower the bar to your mid-chest with forearms vertical, then press up and slightly back over your shoulders.

name: dumbbell bench press
cue: Lie on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand over your chest. Lower them to the sides of your chest with elbows about 45 degrees from your body, then press back up.

name: incline dumbbell press
cue: Set the bench to about 30 degrees. Lower the dumbbells to upper chest level, keeping your wrists stacked over your elbows, then press up.

name: dumbbell floor press
cue: Lie on the floor with knees bent and dumbbells above your chest. Lower until your upper arms touch the floor, pause briefly, then press back up.

name: push-up
cue: Hands slightly wider than shoulders, body in one straight line. Lower your chest to just above the floor with elbows about 45 degrees from your body, then push back up.

name: incline push-up
cue: Place your hands on a bench or counter and keep your body straight. Lower your chest to the edge, then push away. A higher surface makes it easier.

name: machine chest press
cue: Adjust the seat so the handles line up with your mid-chest. Press forward without shrugging, pause, then return slowly until you feel a stretch.

name: dips
cue: On parallel bars, lower until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor, leaning slightly forward to bias the chest, then press back up.

name: cable fly
cue: Stand between two pulleys with a slight bend in your elbows. Bring your hands together in a wide arc in front of your chest, squeeze, then open slowly.

name: dumbbell fly
cue: Lie back holding dumbbells above your chest with soft elbows. Open your arms in a wide arc until you feel a chest stretch, then bring them back together.

name: overhead press
aliases: barbell overhead press|military press|shoulder press barbell|ohp
cue: Hold the bar at collarbone height, squeeze your glutes and brace. Press straight up, moving your head through as the bar passes, and lock out over your mid-foot.

name: dumbbell shoulder press
aliases: dumbbell overhead press|db shoulder press|shoulder press
cue: Hold dumbbells at shoulder height with palms forward. Press them up until your arms are straight above your shoulders without arching your back, then lower slowly.

name: pike push-up
cue: From a downward-dog position with hips high, bend your elbows to lower the top of your head toward the floor, then press back up.

name: lateral raise
aliases: side raise|lateral raises|dumbbell lateral raise|side raises
cue: Hold light dumbbells at your sides with a slight elbow bend. Raise your arms out to shoulder height leading with your elbows, then lower slowly.

name: triceps pushdown
cue: Keep your elbows pinned to your sides and push the handle down until your arms are straight. Control it back up without letting your elbows drift forward.

name: overhead triceps extension
aliases: tricep extension|dumbbell triceps extension|french press|overhead extension
cue: Hold one dumbbell overhead with both hands. Lower it behind your head by bending your elbows, keeping them pointing forward, then extend back up.

name: skull crusher
aliases: lying triceps extension|ez bar skull crusher|skullcrusher
cue: Lie on a bench with the bar above your chest. Bend only at the elbows to lower it toward your forehead, then extend back up.

name: bench dips
cue: Sit on the edge of a bench with hands beside your hips and legs forward. Slide off and lower your body by bending your elbows to about 90 degrees, then press up.

name: diamond push-up
cue: Place your hands close together under your chest so your thumbs and index fingers nearly touch. Lower your chest to your hands, keeping your elbows close, then press up.

name: pull-up
cue: Hang from the bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than your shoulders. Pull your chest toward the bar by driving your elbows down, then lower fully under control.

name: chin-up
cue: Hang with an underhand, shoulder-width grip. Pull until your chin clears the bar, keeping your body still, then lower all the way down.

name: lat pulldown
cue: Sit with your thighs secured and grip the bar just outside shoulder width. Pull it to your upper chest by driving your elbows down, then let it rise slowly.

name: dumbbell pullover
cue: Lie across a bench or on the floor holding one dumbbell above your chest with slightly bent arms. Lower it behind your head in an arc until you feel a stretch in your lats, then pull it back over your chest.

name: band lat pulldown
cue: Anchor a band high, for example over a door. Kneel facing it and pull the band down to your upper chest by driving your elbows down, then return slowly.

name: barbell row
aliases: bent over row|barbell bent over row|bb row|barbell rows
cue: Hinge forward with a flat back and the bar hanging below your shoulders. Pull the bar to your lower ribs, squeeze your shoulder blades, then lower with control.

name: one-arm dumbbell row
aliases: dumbbell row|db row|single arm row|one arm row|dumbbell rows
cue: Support one hand and knee on a bench or sturdy surface. Pull the dumbbell toward your hip, leading with your elbow, then lower it until your arm is straight.

name: seated cable row
cue: Sit tall with a slight knee bend and pull the handle to your lower ribs, squeezing your shoulder blades together. Let your arms extend slowly without rounding your back.

name: inverted row
cue: Lie under a sturdy bar or table edge and grip it with straight arms. Keep your body in one line and pull your chest to the bar, then lower slowly. Check that the surface can hold your weight.

name: band row
cue: Anchor a resistance band at chest height and hold the ends with straight arms. Pull your elbows back until your hands reach your ribs, squeeze, then return slowly.

name: face pull
cue: Set a rope at face height and pull it toward your forehead, spreading the ends apart with elbows high. Squeeze your upper back, then return slowly.

name: rear delt fly
aliases: reverse fly|rear delt raise|bent over reverse fly|rear delt flye
cue: Hinge forward with a flat back and dumbbells hanging down. Raise your arms out to the sides with a slight elbow bend until they are level with your torso, then lower slowly.

name: band pull-apart
aliases: band pull apart|pull aparts|band pull aparts
cue: Hold a band at chest height with straight arms. Pull it apart until it touches your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades, then return slowly.

name: dumbbell curl
aliases: bicep curl|biceps curl|dumbbell biceps curl|curls|bicep curls
cue: Keep your elbows at your sides and curl the dumbbells up with palms facing forward. Squeeze at the top and lower slowly without swinging.

name: hammer curl
cue: Hold dumbbells with palms facing each other and curl up without rotating your wrists. Keep your elbows still and lower slowly.

name: barbell curl
cue: Hold the bar with an underhand shoulder-width grip and curl it toward your chest. Keep your elbows by your sides and avoid leaning back.

name: band curl
cue: Stand on the band with the ends in your hands. Curl up keeping your elbows pinned at your sides, then lower slowly against the resistance.

name: leg curl
aliases: hamstring curl|lying leg curl|seated leg curl|leg curls
cue: Set the pad just above your heels and curl it toward your glutes without lifting your hips. Pause, then return slowly.

name: leg extension
cue: Adjust the pad above your ankles and straighten your knees until your legs are nearly locked out. Squeeze your quads, then lower slowly.

name: standing calf raise
cue: Stand on the edge of a step and rise onto your toes as high as possible. Pause at the top and lower until you feel a full stretch. Hold a dumbbell to make it harder.

name: plank
cue: Rest on your forearms and toes with your body in a straight line. Squeeze your glutes and abs, keep your ribs down, and hold without letting your hips sag.

name: side plank
cue: Lie on your side propped on one forearm with feet stacked. Lift your hips so your body forms a straight line and hold, then switch sides.

name: dead bug
cue: Lie on your back with arms up and knees bent at 90 degrees. Lower the opposite arm and leg toward the floor while keeping your lower back pressed down, then switch.

name: bird dog
cue: On hands and knees, extend one arm forward and the opposite leg back without rotating your hips. Pause, return, and switch sides.

name: hanging knee raise
aliases: hanging leg raise|knee raises|hanging knee raises
cue: Hang from a bar and lift your knees toward your chest by curling your pelvis up. Lower slowly without swinging.

name: cable crunch
cue: Kneel under a high cable holding a rope by your head. Curl your ribs toward your hips, keeping your hips still, then return slowly.

name: crunch
cue: Lie on your back with knees bent and hands by your temples. Curl your shoulders off the floor by contracting your abs, then lower slowly.

name: mountain climbers
cue: From a high plank, drive one knee toward your chest and switch legs quickly while keeping your hips low and shoulders over your hands.

name: brisk walk
cue: Walk fast enough that you can talk but not sing. Aim for 20 to 40 minutes, and use an incline on a treadmill for more effort.

name: jump rope
cue: Stay on the balls of your feet and turn the rope with your wrists, jumping only high enough to clear it. Start with short intervals of 30 to 60 seconds.

name: bike intervals
cue: Alternate 30 to 60 seconds of hard pedalling with 60 to 90 seconds easy, for 10 to 20 minutes total.

name: burpees
cue: Drop into a push-up position, lower your chest, push up, jump your feet back to your hands and jump up. Move at a pace you can keep with good form.
